parsed.explanation: Thin, dated dossier (2011-2018). No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented police/border targeting, facility ban or custody rule, and same-sex conduct is decriminalised — so no tier-1/2 state exposure is established. But there is also no documented acceptance of gender diversity, no operating visitor-facing remedy, and no current trans-specific violence data; 2012 reported no incidents while a 2018 NGO reported some SOGI violence. Documented societal stigma/taboo plus no anti-discrimination recourse mean if outed a visitor faces harassment/service refusal with thin recourse (tier 3), and border, facility, ward and custody practice remain open questions. Absence of LGR/anti-discrimination law is a resident gap, not a direct visitor exposure, and is not heavily deducted. Extrapolating from decriminalisation tempered by stigma, weak protection and dated silence places this a step below the 0.65 acceptance-with-remedy tier.
